newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers' unions keen to negotiate.
newsitem.headline: French truckers' unions keen to negotiate.

text.p: French truck drivers' union leaders said on Friday they were keen to negotiate an end to a 12-day-old strike that is strangling the economy provided the government guaranteed by decree payment for all hours worked.

"We don't want to prolong the strike artificially," said Claude Debons of the biggest union, the Socialist-led CFDT on arriving at the Transport Ministry to sign a deal on early retirement. "The condition for lifting the roadblocks is a guarantee on working hours."

"We have come to seek a clear reply from the government on working time. If we have to work all day, we'll work all day," said Alain Renault, representative of the second largest union among the truckers, the Communist-led CGT.

The unions were due to sign agreements with road haulage employers on retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers with 25 years at the wheel, sick pay, travel expenses and a ban on Sunday driving. But the related issues of pay and hours remained outstanding when talks broke off early on Thursday.

Junior transport minister Anne-Marie Idrac said on Friday the government was prepared to issue a decree defining working hours for truckers within two weeks, after bosses and unions seek agreement the issue in a working group.
Full payment for all hours worked, including unloading time and compulsory rest periods on the road, would be equivalent to a substantial pay rise.
